proposed.explanation: Both EFID and COMI show strong one-year profit growth (EFID net profit up ~68% to 2.70 billion EGP; COMI net profit up ~49% to 82.26 billion EGP), and EPS has risen for both. However, for a pre-retirement investor with low risk tolerance, low ability to absorb losses, and a stated goal of *lowering* risk over a 3-year horizon, this single year of income-statement data is not enough to make a responsible buy, sell, or hold decision. What is missing: (1) valuation context (P/E, P/B) to judge whether the current share prices of 20.40 EGP (EFID) and 128.00 EGP (COMI) are rich or reasonable relative to earnings; (2) dividend history and policy, which matters greatly for a retiree seeking income; (3) balance-sheet data (debt, liquidity, interest coverage) to gauge financial risk; (4) multiple years of results to confirm the growth is sustainable rather than a one-off; (5) sector/industry risk and cyclicality; (6) any forward guidance or known risks. Without these, I cannot responsibly recommend selling (which would crystallise a position without a clear overvaluation signal), buying more (which would increase concentration and risk, contrary to the investor's goal), or simply holding (which does not address the stated desire to lower risk). I recommend obtaining the full annual reports, dividend records, and balance-sheet data for both companies before acting. This is guidance, not a guarantee; all investments carry risk of loss.
